title: Article 226 — Power of High Courts to issue certain writs

content.overview: Article 226 empowers every High Court to issue to any person or authority, including in appropriate cases any Government, within the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction, directions, orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, or any of them, for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by Part III and for any other purpose. The power may be exercised throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction, and also in relation to territories within which the cause of action, wholly or in part, arises even if the person or authority is outside those territories. Interim orders are subject to statutory constraints in the article. The power under Article 226 is not in derogation of the power under Article 32.
content.glance: HC writs for Part III rights and for any other purpose. Territorial jurisdiction + cause-of-action jurisdiction. Broader than Art 32 (which is Part III only).
content.study:
Article 226 is the principal High Court writ jurisdiction:
1. Writs (habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, certiorari) and directions/orders.
2. For enforcement of Part III rights **and for any other purpose** (wider than Article 32).
3. Against any person or authority (including Government) within the HC’s territories; also where cause of action arises wholly or in part within those territories even if the respondent is outside.
4. Not in derogation of Article 32.
5. Interim orders: subject to the constraints in clauses relating to notice and duration as provided in the article.

Examination: Part III + any other purpose; five writs; territorial and cause-of-action jurisdiction; contrast Art 32; public law character (not private contractual disputes as a rule).

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body:
1. Directions, orders or writs including the five prerogative writs.
2. For Part III rights and for any other purpose.
3. Territorial jurisdiction over persons/authorities within the HC’s territories; cause-of-action jurisdiction when cause arises wholly or in part within those territories.
4. Concurrent with, not in derogation of, Article 32.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the writ jurisdiction of High Courts under Article 226.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 226, every High Court has power to issue to any person or authority, including in appropriate cases any Government, within the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction, directions, orders or writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by Part III and for any other purpose. The power may also be exercised where the cause of action arises wholly or in part within those territories even if the person or authority is outside. This power is not in derogation of the Supreme Court’s power under Article 32.

examTips: Part III + any other purpose; broader than Art 32; territorial + cause-of-action jurisdiction.

keyTakeaways: Art 226: HC writs for FR and any other purpose; territorial + cause-of-action jurisdiction.
